sources.name: Norwegian University of Life Sciences (NMBU)
sources.text: Centre for Land Tenure Studies report, Explaining the recent reduction of Indonesia's deforestation: the 40% to 90% range across datasets, the "at least 50%" robust estimate, and the finding that differing definitions create a wide range of figures open to selective use.

sources.name: Mongabay (May 2025)
sources.text: Reporting on the NMBU findings: the 90% official figure for 2015-2021, GFW's 69% for 2016-2023, the 2015 El Nino baseline, Ahmad Dermawan's "not necessarily incorrect" qualification and the Jokowi-term explanation, and the inclusion of commercial acacia plantations in the official forest definition.

sources.name: Global Forest Watch
sources.text: 2024 Tree Cover Loss Data Explained: the SIMONTANA methodology (permanent conversion, 6.25 ha minimum, manual visual inspection, July-June observation year) against UMD/GFW tree cover loss (calendar year, fixed baseline, includes plantations).

sources.name: Mongabay (April 2026)
sources.text: The 66% rise in 2025 deforestation, nickel mining as a driver, and Auriga Nusantara's statement that all datasets are valid under their own methodologies.
